en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Section on the Refutation of Difficulties (Meṇḍakapañha Paṇāmitavagga)
7. The Question on the Worship of the Buddha “Venerable Nāgasena, this was said by the Tathāgata: ‘Ānanda, you should not occupy yourselves with the worship of the Tathāgata’s body.
Yet, on the other hand, it was also said:”
"Worship the relic of him who is worthy of worship;
thus, it is said, you shall go from here to heaven.
If, venerable Nāgasena, it was spoken by the Tathāgata—

If [it is true that] the Tathāgata said, “Ānanda, you need not concern yourselves with the worship of the Tathāgata’s body,” then the statement, “Worship his relics, which are worthy of worship; by doing so, you will go from here to heaven,” must be false.

If, however, the Tathāgata said, “Worship his relics, which are worthy of worship; by doing so, you will go from here to heaven,” then the statement, “Ānanda, you need not concern yourselves with the worship of the Tathāgata’s body,” must also be false.
“This too is a dilemma with two sides that has come to you;
it must be resolved by you. “It was indeed said, Great King, by the Blessed One: ‘Ānanda, you should not be occupied with the worship of the Tathāgata’s remains.
Yet again it was said: ‘Worship his relics, which are worthy of worship; by doing so, you will go from here to heaven. And that was not spoken solely with reference to all the sons of the Conqueror.”
“Ānanda, you need not concern yourselves with the worship of the Tathāgata’s body.
For this, Great King, is not the work of the sons of the Conqueror: namely, worship;

rather, it is the contemplation of formations, wise attention, the practice of the foundations of mindfulness, grasping the core of the object, the battle against the defilements, and the pursuit of one’s own true goal.
This is what must be done by the sons of the Conquerors: worship must be performed for all other gods and humans.

Great King, just as for the princes on earth there must be training in and the performance of elephant-riding, horsemanship, charioteering, archery, swordsmanship, writing, sealing, arithmetic, debate, and warfare;
whereas for the rest—the commoners and the laborers—there must be farming, trade, and cattle-rearing.
In the same way, Great King, this is not the work of the Sons of the Conqueror:

namely, making offerings, the contemplation of formations, appropriate attention, the practice of the foundations of mindfulness, grasping the essence of the object, the battle against the defilements, and the pursuit of one’s own goal.
This is what must be done by the Sons of the Conqueror; as for the rest, making offerings is what must be done by other gods and humans.
Or again, Great King, just as the young brahmins [study] the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, the Athabbana-veda,
the science of marks (lakkhaṇa), history (itihāsa), the Purāṇas, the Nighaṇḍus, the Keṭubhas, the analysis of syllables, word-study, grammar, the paths of speech,
portents, dreams, omens, the sixfold limbs [of the Veda], lunar eclipses, solar eclipses, and the movements of Venus and Rāhu;
Astrology, the battle of the planets, the sound of divine drums, the appearance of meteors, earthquakes, the burning of the quarters, terrestrial and celestial phenomena,
astronomy, Lokāyata philosophy, the wheels of the chariot, the deer-wheel, the intermediate wheel, the production of mixed portents, the cries and calls of birds—
these are the skills to be mastered. For the rest of the commoners— the Vessas and Suddas— farming, trade, and cattle-rearing are the tasks to be performed.
In the same way, Great King, this is not the work of the sons of the Conqueror:

namely, making offerings, the contemplation of formations, wise attention, the practice of the foundations of mindfulness, grasping the core of the object, the battle against the defilements, and the pursuit of one’s own goal.
This is what must be done by the sons of the Conqueror; for all other gods and humans, making offerings is what must be done. Therefore, Great King, [this is the distinction].
The Tathāgata said, “Let these not be occupied with non-work; let these be occupied with work,” and he said,
“Ānanda, you should remain unoccupied with the worship of the Tathāgata’s body.”
“Great King, if the Tathāgata were not to speak thus, the monks, having exhausted even their own bowls and robes, would perform only worship of the Buddha.
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena! It is so; I accept it as you have said.
The seventh dilemma: Worship of the Buddha.
